Dựa vào các tài liệu ISO 21307 và các tài liệu khác hãy xây dựng web về hàn mặt đầu và hàn lồng ống HDPE, PP-R

**Defining the Scope**

I'm now zeroing in on defining the precise scope of this React application. I am outlining the fundamental features needed to expertly guide someone through welding HDPE. Key user tasks, such as material selection and equipment setup, are being prioritized, and I am considering how the expert's knowledge can be effectively structured and presented within the application.


**Focusing on Pipe Welding**

I've shifted focus to welding of PPR pipes, specifically Butt Fusion and Socket Fusion techniques per ISO 21307. I'm imagining a professional, industrial vibe for technicians, engineers, and DIY enthusiasts, emphasizing clean design and safety. The app will feature a landing page with fusion method selection. The Butt Fusion section will contain a step-by-step guide, and I will be developing a parameter calculator with some minor adjustments.


**Adding Socket Fusion Details**

I'm now incorporating detailed content for Socket Fusion within the application. This includes clear explanations, heating depth and time charts using standard data, and a step-by-step guide. I am also working on Gemini AI integration with a "Virtual Welding Expert" chat to assist with standards, troubleshooting, and safety. I'm focusing on the React 18+ tech stack with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide React, and Google GenAI SDK.


**Outlining Component Structure**

I am now structuring the React application's components. I'm establishing the core layout with `App.tsx`, `Header.tsx`, and `Footer.tsx`. Key functionalities will reside in `ButtFusion.tsx`, `SocketFusion.tsx`, and `AIChat.tsx`, which will call `geminiService.ts` for AI integration. I plan to separate all the code into clear logical units.

**Implementing Visual Style**

I am now focusing on refining the application's visual design using Tailwind CSS. I'm adopting an industrial color palette with blue (background), safety orange (warnings), and white/gray (content). I'm planning a responsive grid layout with step cards and a sticky sidebar for the AI chat and tools.

**Mapping Implementation Steps**

I've just finalized the step-by-step implementation plan. Step 1 will cover setup and metadata, including `metadata.json`, `index.html`, and `index.tsx`. Step 2 involves creating shared types via `types.ts`, including welding parameters and chat data structures. Step 3 will establish `geminiService.ts` for the Gemini API. Step 4 will focus on component implementation.


**Defining App Logic**

I'm now focusing on the core app structure; `App.tsx` will handle view switching. I'm finalizing the structure, noting the `Header` and `AIChat` components are simple navigations, with `SocketFusion` being table-centric and `ButtFusion` calculator-focused. I will soon be writing code, particularly the Gemini service with the new Google GenAI SDK and the model `gemini-3-flash-preview`. The system prompt for AI has been drafted. The butt fusion calculator will be simplified for the MVP.


**Calculating Pressure Values**

I'm now implementing the cylinder area to gauge pressure calculation for the butt fusion calculator. I've also integrated a socket fusion heating time lookup table, referencing standard diameter sizes. In addition, I have verified the project meets all constraints, including the correct Gemini API usage. Lastly, I'm constructing the XML representation, and ensuring the interface and AI will be in Vietnamese ("xây dựng web về hàn...").

**Expanding Calculator Functionality**

I'm currently focused on the Butt Fusion calculator's update. The main task is straightforward: I need to add functionality to choose between SDR and PN values for pipe specifications, expanding beyond the current SDR-only input.


**Visualize the Fusion Process**

I'm now shifting gears to the visualization component. I'm leaning toward a custom SVG chart for the pressure-vs-time graph in the butt fusion calculator. I need to figure out the best approach to import libraries or use native elements. The data structure will be straightforward - a simple step chart. Currently, I'm analyzing the existing import map to make sure I do not accidentally import `recharts` if it is not already being imported.


**Implementing Graph Details**

I've decided to add `recharts` to `index.html` to enhance the visual appeal of the graph. My focus is now on updating `ButtFusion.tsx`. I'm implementing an "Input Mode: SDR / PN" selector and mapping standard PN values to SDR for HDPE. I also plan to add a material selector for PE100/PE80, as this impacts the mapping accuracy. Finally, I'm working on the welding cycle graph visualization (Pressure vs Time).


**Defining Welding Cycle Stages**

I've broken down the welding cycle stages. It's now clear that it includes bead-up, heat soak, change-over, fusing, and cooling phases. Each stage has distinct pressure and time characteristics. I'm leveraging `recharts` for visualization, and plan to represent this cycle visually.


**Constructing Graph Data**

My current focus is on building the data structure for the welding cycle graph, keeping `recharts` in mind. I need to generate an array of objects for the chart. I've defined the key points: start, bead-up, heat soak, changeover, joining, and cooling. I have the pressure values for each and their corresponding times. Now, I'm working on how to represent this data effectively in the graph. I believe a scatter chart with connected lines is the best approach. I also need to make sure the time axis is either cumulative or categorical.


**Refining Visualization Approach**

I'm now refining the visualization approach for the welding cycle. The end of heat soak is at `(10 + heatSoakTime, 0)` and the start of changeover is at `(10 + heatSoakTime + changeOverTime, 0)`. The fusing ramp up stage is at `(10 + heatSoakTime + changeOverTime + 1, P_fuse)`. The end cooling stage is at `(10 + heatSoakTime + changeOverTime + 1 + coolingTime*60, P_fuse)`. I need to convert cooling time from minutes to seconds for the graph. I'm leaning toward a schematic approach because of the large range in time, using a categorical X-axis in `Recharts` for "Stage" rather than raw seconds. Or, I may try an area chart, because the user is after a visual profile of the ISO curve.


**Implementing ISO Cycle Visualization**

I'm now focusing on implementing the ISO cycle visualization using either an `AreaChart` or `LineChart` from `recharts`, potentially with stepped lines. I have the standard cycle points, including bead-up, heat soak, change-over, joining, and cooling, with their corresponding pressure levels. I'll need to define the PE_Material and related values. I've also added recharts to `index.html` already. Now, I'm working on the `ButtFusion.tsx` file for the new logic and graph. I'm focusing on defining the chart data structure to represent the different stages, ensuring it aligns with the ISO diagram. I will need to use an array of objects for the chart. I need to make sure I am using the right material (PE80/PE100) and the right SDR/PN value.


**Designing Chart Data**

I'm now building the schematic chart data, focused on visualizing pressure profiles across the five phases, accounting for time scale differences. To ensure readability, I'll generate a "synthetic" time axis for visualization, displaying actual times in labels and tooltips, which will be much better. This approach will allow us to represent the process shape effectively. I'm prioritizing the visual representation of the process shape to conform to ISO 21307 diagrams, where time axes are often broken.


**Refining Cycle Data**

I'm now refining the data structure for the welding cycle. I'm focusing on "Bead-up", "Heat Soak", "Change-over", "Ramp-up", and "Cooling" phases, with pressure on the Y-axis. The data points will define these stages effectively. Thinking through the chart, I've decided `recharts` can handle categorical axes well. I'm now refining the UI for the inputs, specifically the material and standard (SDR/PN) selectors, including how to dynamically show the appropriate SDR/PN dropdown. I'm also preparing for the XML output. I'm noting the difference between ISO 21307 (current focus) and DVS 2207, mentioned in initial instructions.


**Refining SDR/PN Mapping**

I'm working on refining the SDR/PN mapping within `ButtFusion.tsx`. I've created a more robust lookup table for SDR values, including standard values like 41, 33, 26, etc. and associated them with their respective PN values. This update will ensure accurate calculations and provide the user with clear and precise data visualizations. I'm also preparing for the XML output, to show users the data in their preferred format.


**Implementing SDR/PN Logic**

I'm now integrating the SDR/PN calculation logic. I've decided to maintain `sdr` within the `params` state for calculation simplicity. I'm focusing on handling the user input for PN, and then using that to determine the SDR value for the calculation, and updating the state accordingly.


**Defining UI State**

I'm now refining the UI state within `ButtFusion.tsx` to include `inputMode` (SDR/PN), `selectedPN`, and `material`. I've added a state variable for each, which will determine the user's choice and the resulting calculations and display on the UI.


**Finalizing Chart Implementation**

I'm now implementing a `CustomChart` component in `ButtFusion.tsx` for the schematic ISO cycle visualization, and have started on the custom tick formatter for the X-axis. I'm focusing on the X-axis labels to accurately display actual times for each phase, while the chart uses a synthetic time axis for better visual representation.


**Switching to SVG**

I've decided to abandon `recharts` for a native SVG implementation. Considering the project's requirements, specifically the ISO 21307 graph, an SVG approach is lighter, more robust, and offers precise control. This avoids library dependency issues and ensures the visualization looks exactly as expected. The graph will be a poly-line shape. I'm focusing on defining the SVG canvas size (600x300), margins, and coordinate system.

I'm now generating chart data to visualize the butt fusion process, using `Recharts`.
